name: Fog-Desolation
description: Fog-Desolation is a tiny, airless barren world named with bitter irony by its discoverers, who noted that its surface dust occasionally rises in electrostatic suspension to create a fog-like haze despite the total absence of atmosphere. The surface is a wasteland of impact craters, glass plains, and fine regolith that shifts in slow, ghostly waves driven by static charge from solar wind interactions. The temperature extremes between sunlit and shadowed faces are savage.

The electrostatic dust fog gives the surface an unsettling quality, as particles hover motionlessly at various heights, creating the impression of a frozen mist. Walking through the suspended dust causes it to part and slowly reform, like moving through still water. Without atmosphere, there is no sound, and the visual strangeness of the hovering dust combined with the absolute silence creates an experience many survey teams describe as profoundly disorienting.

An escape pod debris field on the equatorial plain tells a story of disaster. Seven pods are scattered across a two-kilometer area, all bearing the same ship registry but showing different impact angles, suggesting they were ejected during an emergency rather than a controlled evacuation. The pods are empty, their supplies depleted, and scratched marks on the interior walls of two pods suggest extended occupancy. No remains have been found.

Fog-Desolation has no resources of note and no strategic value. It persists in navigational databases primarily as a cautionary waypoint and the site of an unsolved mystery. The escape pod occupants clearly survived landing but equally clearly did not survive long-term on an airless world. How they left, if they left, is unknown. The hovering dust preserves their landing marks and the trails they made between pods, footprints frozen in electrostatic suspension for decades.
